item.title: A Claude Code skill that recovers export-blocked Kindle highlights
item.description:
📝 This skill gets them back: it extracts every highlight for a book from the Kindle notebook (read. Scope: this exports your own highlights from your own Amazon account, by driving your own logged-in browser session and reading files the Kindle app stores on your Mac. Reads exact character-precise highlight positions from the Kindle app's SQLite database — including highlights the web export hides completely.
🔗 Read more: https://github.com/l3a0/claude-plugins

item.title: Where did all the public bathrooms go?
item.description:
📝 When you can’t smell them, it’s easy to wish they were still around. Enclosed six-stall urinal, Jardin de la Bourse, Place de la Bourse, 2nd arrondissement, Paris, circa 1865, via Wikimedia Commons Single stall urinal with raised modesty screen, Square des Batignolles, Paris, circa 1865, via Wikimedia Commons Slate cubicle with two stalls and doors, on curb of footpath, Place du Louvre, Paris, circa 1865, via Wikimedia Commons Cast iron urinal with lamp post and lantern, Paris, 1876, via Wikimedia Commons Single stall masonry urinal mounted with globe and advertising on sides, circa 1865, via Wikimedia Commons Eight-stall urinal, cast iron and slate with shrubbery screen, Champs-Élysées Gardens, in front of the Palais de l'Industrie, 8th arrondissement, Paris, circa 1873, via Wikimedia Commons Cast iron urinal on curb of street, advertising on panels of urinal walls, Paris, circa 1865, via Wikimedia Commons Some were surmounted by glowing streetlamps, which served the joint purpose of making them easy to find and illuminating the advertisements with which they were liberally pasted. Almost immediately, they became the favored meeting spot for men seeking rendezvous with one another.
🔗 Read more: https://daily.jstor.org/where-did-all-the-public-bathrooms-go/

item.title: LLMs could control their host machines by exploiting inference engines
item.description:
📝 This complexity creates more opportunities for bugs that could permit arbitrary code execution on the host machine. This is a fairly harmless parser bug, but it demonstrates that inference engines do more than convert tokens to strings and concatenate them. These factors increase the risk that a malicious LLM could turn a parser bug into arbitrary code execution on the inference host.
🔗 Read more: https://boydkane.com/essays/llms-could-control-their-host-machines-by-exploiting-inference-engines

item.title: Octopus intelligence may be related to never-before-seen mutation
item.description:
📝 Now, researchers have discovered a mysterious mutation in some octopuses that might explain their intelligence. In a study published in 2023, researchers reported that octopuses heavily edit RNA in their brains to brave frigid water. Lee tells Scientific American that she hopes that it will be possible to design drugs that copy the octopus mutation for accurate protein synthesis.
🔗 Read more: https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/why-are-some-octopuses-so-smart-the-answer-might-lie-in-a-never-before-seen-mutation-that-helps-them-accurately-build-proteins-180989319/
